text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. - - - -
-- Growing food production has enabled Vietnam to focus on food security, a conference timed to coincide with World Food Week was told.

-- An American military delegation led by Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Kurt Campbell paid a visit to Vietnam last week. Campbell discussed matters of common interest with officials from Vietnam's ministries of defence anbd foreign affairs.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has sent an urgent message to Mekong Delta People's Committees and relevaqnt agencies asking them to devise ways of protecting lives and property in the latest floods.
-- Vietnam's beekeppers predicted on Tuesday that the country's honey output will see a dramatic increase over the coming years.

-- The ground-breaking ceremony for the construction of the Mai Son paper plant in Son La province was held on Tuesday. To be equipped with Chinese equipment and facilities, the plant will have an annual capacity of 1,500 tonnes a year and will be fully operational by January, 1998. - - - -
-- A national conference on reinforcing the Communist Party was held by the party's central organizational commission.

-- The Vietnam Coal Corporation sold more than 6.3 million tonnes of coal, including 2.53 million tonnes as exports, in the first nine months of this year, up 24 percent from the same period of last year.
-- Vietnam is facing a shortage of 120,000 teachers in this school year. - - - -
-- State budget revenues in the first nine months reached 63.3 percent of the target for the whole year, up 14.8 percent from the same period last year. - - - -
-- The first 22 foreign non-governmental organizations were granted lisences to operate in Vietnam.
-- A three-day course for officials of Hanoi's Police force on the resolution of the Eighth Communist Party Congress began on Monday.
-- The international tennis tournament, Hanoi Open 1996, started on Tuesday. - - - -
